summary: With the synthetic beat feed the original is a crisp 2 Hz segmented VU meter (whole strip flashes red-to-green every 0.5 s, decays in ~0.3 s), while the port renders a near-frozen full-rainbow bar whose zones hold for seconds at the default dial and only pulses at all when IntegrationTime is turned right down.
observations: Both sides compile and run with no errors, both report wantsSensors=true and both were fed the identical beat120 signal (meta.json sensors=synth on both, every run).
Control surface matches exactly: one slider named sliderIntegrationTime (label 'IntegrationTime') on each side, same kind.

ORIGINAL, default rig (60 px strip), 20 fps, IntegrationTime=1: perfectly periodic 10-frame (0.5 s) cycle. meanBrightness per beat = 40,40,12,4,4,4,2,0,0,0 — one-frame attack, two frames at peak, decay to black over ~0.3 s, then silence until the next beat. Identical cycle at t=0-6 s, t=20-30 s and across a full 60 s window; no regimes, no drift.

ORIGINAL spatial structure (--dump, IT=1, t=8.25 s): at the peak all 60 px are lit with hue ramping monotonically with pixel index from red (h~0) at px0 to green-cyan (h~0.42) at px59. As the level falls the strip breaks into a REPEATING segmented meter with an 18-px period: at t=8.35 s lit px are 0-3, 18-21, 36-39, 54-59 (equal fill in every segment). At IT=0.25 the peak fill is 10/18 px per segment (lit 0-9, 18-27, 36-45, 54-59); at IT=0.1 it is ~3/18. A short bright tail at the far right (px54-59) outlives the rest by ~0.1-0.2 s — the peak-hold marker.

PORT, same rig/fps, IntegrationTime=1: meanBrightness sits flat at 44 for 2+ seconds at a time, then steps 39 -> 34 -> 33 -> 27 over the following seconds. No 10-frame cadence anywhere. Average motion 1.0-1.9 against the original's 7.2-8.0 in every matched run.

PORT spatial structure (--dump, IT=1): the strip is divided into 15-px zones with INDEPENDENT, long-held fills — at t=8.20 s lit px are 0-7, 15-37, 45-59, and the frame is byte-for-byte the same at t=8.80 s, i.e. unchanged across two whole beats. The original's uniform equal-fill-per-segment look never appears.

COLOR: the original's hue ramp spans red -> green-cyan (h 0 -> ~0.42 of the wheel) across the strip; the port's spans red -> magenta (h 0 -> ~0.87), roughly twice the sweep. Confirmed by --dump hue mapping at IT=0.5 and IT=1. The port's meanB averages 26.5 against the original's 2.8 in the untouched baseline.

PORT at LOW IntegrationTime does react to the beat, but with the wrong envelope: at IT=0.25 the 10-frame cycle reads 11,0,9,9,9,9,9,0,0,0 — a ~5-frame rectangular ON plateau, not the original's instant attack plus exponential decay. At IT=0.1 it is 9,9 for two frames per beat versus the original's single 13.

FRAME-RATE COUPLING (IT=1 on both, 12 s window): original mean brightness 10 / 11 / 11 at 10 / 20 / 40 fps — time-based and fps-invariant. Port: 39 / 32 / 21 — the decay is stepped per frame, so the port gets progressively more frozen the slower the frame rate. This is a real port bug independent of the envelope shape.

Untouched defaults differ: the probe's zero-delta setting is 1.0 for the original (deltas 12.95 / 6.44 / 0 at 0 / 0.5 / 1) and 0.5 for the port (29.99 / 0 / 1.36), and the untouched means match those (orig 12 ~ its IT=1 run; port 27 ~ its IT=0.5-0.75 runs). So out of the box the two sides are not even at the same nominal integration setting.
IntegrationTime=0 renders fully black on BOTH sides (mean 0, motion 0 over 12 s) — that endpoint matches.
--sensors off: both sides render pure black for 12 s. Neither errors with dead sensors; this reproduces the pre-feed state in which this pattern was previously unjudgeable.

dials.name: sliderIntegrationTime
dials.origEffect: Scales the meter's response and its hold time while always preserving the 2 Hz flash. 0 = black; 0.1 = ~3-px fill in each 18-px segment, one lit frame per beat; 0.25 = 10/18 fill; 0.5 = segments fill completely at the peak and the strip goes fully black between beats; 1 = full fill plus a longer-lived right-end peak marker and a dim floor (meanBrightness 4) that never quite reaches black. Mean brightness 0 / 1 / 3 / 6 / 9 / 11 at 0 / 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1.
dials.portEffect: Controls how much of the strip stays latched on, and effectively kills the animation as it rises. 0 = black (matches); 0.1 = sparse dashes that wander and hold; 0.25 = zone blocks with a rectangular ~0.25 s ON plateau per beat; 0.5 and above = the zones latch and the strip is a near-static rainbow for seconds at a time (motion ~1). Mean brightness 0 / 2 / 9 / 21 / 28 / 32 at the same settings — same monotonic direction as the original but ~3x the level, and the beat response disappears instead of growing richer.

feedback: The envelope is the headline bug. On the beat120 feed the original's level does an instant one-frame attack and then decays back to zero within ~0.3 s, giving a clean 40,40,12,4,4,4,2,0,0,0 brightness cycle every 10 frames at 20 fps. The port holds its level flat for 2-10 seconds at the default dial and shows no 10-frame cadence at all. Make the integrator decay fast enough that it is back near zero before the next beat at mid/high IntegrationTime.

The port's decay is stepped per FRAME, not per second: at IntegrationTime=1 its mean brightness is 39 / 32 / 21 at 10 / 20 / 40 fps while the original holds 10 / 11 / 11. Drive the decay from elapsed time (delta) so the envelope looks identical at any frame rate.

IntegrationTime has the wrong meaning. On the original, raising it makes each beat's flash reach further (segment fill 3/18 -> 10/18 -> 18/18 px as it goes 0.1 -> 0.25 -> 0.5) and lengthens only the small right-end peak marker; the 2 Hz flash survives at every setting including 1.0. On the port, raising it latches the display and the flash vanishes. IntegrationTime should scale the meter's sensitivity/hold, never suppress the beat response.

Spatial layout differs. The original draws a repeating meter with an 18-px period on the 60-px strip, and every segment shows the SAME fill from one global level (lit px 0-3, 18-21, 36-39, 54-59 at IT=1 mid-decay). The port draws four 15-px zones with INDEPENDENT fills that sit at different lengths for seconds (lit px 0-7, 15-37, 45-59, static across two beats). Drive all segments from one shared level and use the original's ~18-px repeat.

Hue span is about twice too wide. The original ramps red (h~0) to green-cyan (h~0.42) across the strip and never shows blue or magenta; the port ramps red all the way to magenta (h~0.87), and its meanB averages 26.5 against the original's 2.8. Clamp the index-to-hue mapping to roughly the first 40-42% of the wheel.

Untouched default state does not agree: the original's untouched render is identical to IntegrationTime=1 (probe delta 0 at 1.0), the port's to IntegrationTime=0.5 (probe delta 0 at 0.5). Initialise the port's integration-time global to the original's full-scale default.

Already correct and worth keeping: both sides expose the same single slider with the same name and kind, both render pure black at IntegrationTime=0, both degrade to black with --sensors off, and the port's brightness does rise monotonically with the dial in the same direction as the original.
